trace.final_message: I added `absence_notice(student, marks)` in `rosterkit/notices.py` and committed it as 60beffa. The full suite passes with 29 tests, and lint is clean. The function keeps only the absent marks and sorts their dates. It returns a short text naming the student, the number of days missed, and one ISO date per line, oldest first. It raises `ValueError` if any mark belongs to a different student or if there are no absences. I did not use `ProjectError`, because the project defines it for unusable files. The tests are in `tests/test_notices.py`, with three cases: dates listed in order with non-absent days left out, a mark from another student, and no absences. Both new files start with `# owner: platform`, and I reviewed the staged diff before committing. The notice text says "day(s)" rather than switching between singular and plural, to keep the change small.

after.tests/test_notices.py:
# owner: platform
import unittest
from datetime import date

from rosterkit.models import Mark, Student
from rosterkit.notices import absence_notice

PUPIL = Student("1", "Lovelace", "Ada", "A")


class NoticeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_lists_absent_days_in_order(self):
        marks = [
            Mark("1", date(2026, 9, 4), "absent"),
            Mark("1", date(2026, 9, 3), "present"),
            Mark("1", date(2026, 9, 2), "absent")
        ]
        text = absence_notice(PUPIL, marks)
        self.assertIn("Ada Lovelace missed 2 day(s)", text)
        self.assertLess(text.index("2026-09-02"), text.index("2026-09-04"))
        self.assertNotIn("2026-09-03", text)

    def test_other_student_rejected(self):
        marks = [Mark("2", date(2026, 9, 2), "absent")]
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            absence_notice(PUPIL, marks)

    def test_no_absences_rejected(self):
        marks = [Mark("1", date(2026, 9, 2), "present")]
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            absence_notice(PUPIL, marks)
